stem.en: Waves have cut an arch through a headland. What finally brings down the top of the arch?

text.en: Strong wind blowing through the opening

feedback.en: No. Wind does not bring the top down. The rock falls.

text.en: Storm waves striking the top from above

feedback.en: No. Waves work low down, near the foot of the rock.

text.en: Sand piling up on top until it is crushed

feedback.en: No. Nothing piles up there. The waves take rock away from below.

text.en: Gravity, after waves cut the rock below

feedback.en: Yes. The waves take away the rock beneath, and gravity brings the top down.

explanation.en: The waves cut away the rock underneath. The top of the arch then collapses because of gravity, and it leaves a tall sea stack standing in the water.

hints.en: What pulls down anything that is left unsupported?
